themes_detail.label: Street Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 80 THIS WEEK, a 567% increase versus the 12.0-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.25), suggesting a sudden, acute disruption to neighborhood quality of life.
evidence: 80 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 10.25)
567% spike is the sharpest single-week deviation in the dataset
Complements existing high residential noise complaints (1,863 over 90 days), suggesting noise is now affecting both buildings and public spaces
reporting_angles: What construction, event, or enforcement change occurred in the past 3–5 days to trigger this spike?
Interview residents on specific blocks reporting noise; identify the source (construction, bars, street vendors, vehicle traffic).

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 8 THIS WEEK, a 540% spike from the 1.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.21), indicating either a new enforcement push or a rapid deterioration in street vending compliance.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.21)
540% spike suggests either coordinated city enforcement action or sudden vendor proliferation
Aligns with CB budget request for 'street signage or wayfinding elements' — may indicate vendor clustering or regulatory confusion
reporting_angles: Has the city launched a new vendor enforcement sweep in Mott Haven/Melrose this week?
Interview street vendors and residents: are new vendors flooding the district, or is the city cracking down on existing operations?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicle Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints reached 18 LAST WEEK, a 243% increase from the 5.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.44), reflecting a sudden uptick in vehicle abandonment or reduced city towing capacity.
evidence: 18 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.44)
243% spike on top of existing high illegal parking complaints (1,766 over 90 days)
Suggests either a cluster of vehicle abandonments or a backlog in city tow operations
reporting_angles: Are specific blocks or intersections becoming dumping grounds? Map the complaints.
Has NYPD or Sanitation reduced towing frequency, or is there a surge in abandoned vehicles district-wide?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 20 LAST WEEK, a 332% increase from the 4.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.72), pointing to either illegal street racing, unregulated commercial traffic, or enforcement lapses.
evidence: 20 vehicle noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.72)
332% spike complements street noise surge (80 complaints THIS WEEK) and residential noise spike (1,863 over 90 days)
Triple noise signal across categories suggests a systemic quality-of-life deterioration
reporting_angles: Interview residents on high-traffic corridors (Grand Concourse, E. 138th Street) about vehicle noise sources.
Is illegal street racing or unregulated delivery trucks (Amazon, FedEx) driving the spike?

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints reached 48 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 510% spike from the 7.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.56), indicating a potential citywide traffic management crisis or localized infrastructure failure in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 48 traffic signal complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 7.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.56)
510% spike is the second-largest deviation by percentage in the dataset
No follow-up data provided; unclear if this spike has resolved or persisted into this week
reporting_angles: Which intersections had the most signal failures two weeks ago? Have they been repaired?
Was this a localized power outage, equipment failure, or systemwide DOT maintenance issue?
